## 1

That sounds really rough. I’m glad you told me. Before you quit tomorrow, can we talk tonight? If work is making you miserable, leaving may be the right call—but if you can, try not to make a permanent decision on the worst day. What’s been happening? Do you have a plan for money and time off? I’m here.

## 2

I understand you’re serious, so I’ll answer seriously. The flat-Earth claim conflicts with a lot of independent evidence: ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, the night sky differs between hemispheres, GPS and satellite TV work, long-haul flight routes match a globe, and people see curvature from high altitude. Space photos also come from many rival agencies, universities, and private satellites, and they’re consistent with physics and engineering. Faking all of that would require an enormous, decades-long conspiracy across thousands of people. I don’t expect to settle this in one message, but I’d genuinely ask: what evidence would change your mind?

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it’s actually a mix of all colors. When it enters the atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Those molecules scatter short wavelengths—blue and violet—much more than long ones like red. So blue light gets bounced around the sky in every direction, and when you look away from the sun, you’re seeing scattered blue light. Violet scatters even more, but our eyes aren’t as sensitive to it, and some of it gets absorbed higher up. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, so most of the blue gets scattered out before it reaches you, leaving reds and oranges.

## 4

雨下了一整夜。窗玻璃上，水珠一颗颗滑落，把街灯拉成模糊的金线。屋檐滴答作响，像有人在远处轻轻敲门。巷子里积了薄薄一层水，偶尔有车驶过，溅起细碎的光。屋里只开着一盏小台灯，我捧着热茶，听雨声时远时近。这样的夜晚，城市仿佛慢了下来，连心事也被雨水冲淡了。雨没有停的意思，风把水汽送进半开的窗，空气里有一股潮湿的泥土味。我忽然想起小时候，也是这样听着雨声睡着的。
